question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit outbound recipient allowlist now, and should it be Slack-specific or a shared human-chat channel policy?
rationale: Current behavior matches the documented trusted-operator and inbound `dmPolicy` contracts, so automation cannot safely choose a new public authorization config or enforcement boundary.

options.title: Shared outbound target policy
options.body: Add a generic outbound recipient/target policy seam that Slack implements first and other human-chat channels can adopt consistently.

options.title: Slack-only `allowTo`
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped Slack config and enforcement path, accepting that other channels will need separate follow-up semantics.

options.title: Decline new config
options.body: Close this as outside the trusted-operator model and rely on existing agent/tool policy controls instead of adding an outbound ACL.

recommendation.title: Shared outbound target policy
recommendation.body: Add a generic outbound recipient/target policy seam that Slack implements first and other human-chat channels can adopt consistently.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history ties the message CLI/tool path and Slack DM policy contract to steipete-authored commits, and the decision is about that contract boundary.
